result.rule: Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use end events for terminal outcomes. An end event has no outgoing sequence flow and is not the target of a message flow.
Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.

result.rule: When the description explicitly states what triggers the process or what outcome terminates it: Label the corresponding start or end event with a concise, faithful description of that stated trigger or outcome rather than a generic label.
When the description explicitly states the outcome that terminates the process: Label the end event to reflect that stated outcome; do not use an unstated or different outcome.

When the description states that the process begins when an incoming communication or request occurs, without describing separate work to receive it: Represent that occurrence with a suitable start event; model a separate receipt activity only when the description states that receiving it is work to be performed.
